If you're building something new right now, I'd bet your week looks a lot like this. 

You get home from the job that pays the bills, open the laptop, and do the same thing you did last night, answering the same customer question, fixing the same page, sending the same follow-up to someone who probably won't reply, while everyone online seems to be announcing their big launch.

It feels like nothing is happening.

I know that feeling. We started Quest making protein bars by hand in a small kitchen. We had no idea if anyone would care. Nobody was clapping. There was no launch moment. There was just the next batch.

I wish someone had told me back then that boredom is what progress feels like from the inside.

Answer that customer’s question one more time and you learn a little more about what's really bugging people. Fix the landing page again and it gets a little easier to buy from you. If you keep going, one of those reps turns into the thing people pay for. If you stop, you never find out which one it was.

Quest Nutrition grew 57,000% in three years. I still almost torched the company trusting my gut over a simple test.

California was in a brutal drought. Almonds take a lot of water to grow, and they were in almost every bar we made.

We saw the problem coming.

Where we screwed up was deciding how big to bet on being right.

We signed huge contracts to lock in our almond supply before things got worse. 

The logic made sense: if the drought continued, almonds would get harder to source and more expensive.

But we weren’t just betting on the drought.

We were betting on exactly how bad it would get, how long it would last, what would happen to prices, and how much inventory we’d need.

We ended up walking away from some of those contracts. It cost us A LOT of money.

If I were making that call today, I’d make AI pressure-test the bet before I signed anything.

Copy this:

[BEGIN PROMPT]

Here’s what I believe will happen: [trend + evidence]

Here’s the move I want to make because of it: [cost, commitment, timeline]

Assume I’m directionally right. Now try to break the bet.

1. WHAT AM I MISSING?
 What assumptions am I treating like facts?

2. HOW DO I STILL LOSE?
 Show me how I could be right about the trend and wrong about timing, magnitude, price, demand, or execution.

3. WHAT’S THE DOWNSIDE?
 Give me painful and catastrophic scenarios. Estimate money lost, time to recover, and what else breaks.

4. MAKE THE BET SMALLER.
 Give me the smallest reversible move that still protects the upside.

5. TELL ME WHEN TO BET MORE OR WALK.
 Give me measurable signals, thresholds, or dates. No vague feelings.

If you can access current data, use it and cite it. Flag anything you can’t verify.

Don’t reassure me. Try to break the decision.

[END PROMPT]

AI won’t make uncertainty disappear. It can force you to see where you’ve confused a good prediction with a good bet.
